name: MINDSTORES: Memory-Informed Neural Decision Synthesis for Task-Oriented Reinforcement in Embodied Systems
venue: arXiv preprint (arXiv:2501.19318, cs.AI); submitted 31 Jan 2025, last revised 3 Jun 2025 (v4). No peer-reviewed venue identified as of mid-2026.
authors_affiliation: Anirudh Chari* and Suraj Reddy* (equal contribution), Aditya Tiwari, Richard Lian, Brian Zhou. arXiv lists affiliations as MIT (Chari, Reddy, Lian), Illinois Mathematics and Science Academy (Tiwari), and Harvard University (Zhou); the project page lists all authors under a37.ai.
code_url: No dedicated public code repository confirmed. The project page (https://a37research.github.io/mindstores/) links 'Code' to the org page https://github.com/orgs/a37research/repositories rather than a specific named repo. [uncertain]
task_domain: Embodied planning / decision-making: LLM high-level planning for an embodied agent in an open-world Minecraft environment (MineDojo), with a low-level behavior-cloning controller executing actions.
problem_setting: Interactive, online, single-agent embodied planning in the open-world MineDojo (Minecraft) simulator. The LLM acts as a zero-shot high-level planner ('brain') that decomposes goals into step-by-step plans, while a behavior-cloning controller ('body') maps plans to 42 discrete low-level actions. No model fine-tuning; learning happens entirely through an accumulating natural-language experience database. Supervision is the environment's task-completion reward/done signal (self-supervised via outcomes); each task evaluated over 30 trials with randomized initial states (seed 42). Long-horizon tasks (episodes 3,000-12,000 steps) with irreversible-error dynamics and task dependencies (e.g., stone tools required before iron mining).
what_is_retrieved: Past experiences stored as natural-language (state, task, plan, outcome) tuples; also LLM-generated insights synthesized from those retrieved experiences. Both successful and failed past episodes are stored and retrievable.
retrieval_grounding: GROWING / episodic memory the agent writes during deployment. The (state,task,plan,outcome) experience database is built online from the agent's own interactions; it is not a static external corpus.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k similarity retrieval objective. The system retrieves the k most similar past experiences (optimal k=5; tested k=1,3,5,10,20) ranked by weighted cosine similarity; there is no notion of recovering a complete minimal set or precision-driven variable-size selection.
retrieval_unit: A (state, task, plan, outcome) experience tuple — i.e., a case (problem-context-solution-result) represented as natural-language paragraphs. Effectively a full episode/trajectory-level experience record rather than a token snippet or single demo.
index_source: Growing memory, online/test-time-induced. The database starts empty (or per-task small, e.g., 26 entries for Wooden Door) and grows from the agent's own executed episodes during deployment (e.g., to 355 entries for Minecart in the continuous-building experiment).
index_structure_topology: Flat vector index. Each of state/task/plan/outcome is embedded with Sentence-BERT (all-MiniLM-L6-v2, treated as 768-dim, L2-normalized) and stored in a FAISS IndexFlatL2 (flat L2 / cosine-similarity) index. No graph or hierarchical structure.
retriever_type: Dense retriever (off-the-shelf sentence-embedding similarity search). Sentence-BERT embeddings + FAISS cosine/L2 nearest-neighbor search.
retriever_learning_signal: None (off-the-shelf). The retriever uses a frozen pretrained Sentence-BERT encoder with fixed manually-set field weights (lambda_s=0.4, lambda_t=0.4, lambda_p=0.2); it is not trained or learned via any task/LM/RL signal.
query_construction: Raw natural-language descriptions of the current state and task form the query keys; for outcome prediction the proposed plan is added. Similarity is computed as a weighted sum over fields (state, task, and optionally plan), each embedded by the same sentence transformer. State/task descriptions and the plan are themselves produced by LLM prompts over the structured environment JSON.
query_granularity: Two-level retrieval. (1) State/task-level retrieval (weights on s and t) to inform plan generation; (2) plan-conditioned retrieval (weights on s, t, p) to predict the proposed plan's outcome before execution.
when_to_retrieve: Iterative. Retrieval is invoked at plan-generation time (state/task neighbors) and again inside the plan-refinement loop for outcome prediction (plan neighbors), repeated each time the plan is revised until predicted success, and re-triggered for each new sub-task within the observe-retrieve-synthesize-act-log cycle.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule tied to the planning loop: retrieve at each new sub-task/state for plan generation, and retrieve again to predict outcomes whenever a candidate plan is (re)generated. The refinement loop continues (re-retrieving and revising) while the predicted outcome is not 'success'. There is no learned router, token-confidence, or attention-based trigger.
reranking: None. A single weighted-cosine-similarity top-k ranking is used; no separate reranking stage (no cross-encoder, RRF, or instruction-tuned reranker).
retrieved_context_refinement: LLM insight synthesis (a form of reason-over-documents distillation): the LLM analyzes the retrieved k experiences to produce 'insights' about common failure modes to avoid, successful strategies to adapt, and environmental dynamics, which are then injected alongside the raw retrieved experiences into the plan-generation prompt. No explicit compression, distractor filtering, or decompose-recompose beyond this analysis step.
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation plus LLM-based case adaptation. Retrieved experiences and synthesized insights condition the LLM's plan generation; retrieved similar past plans/outcomes drive an outcome-prediction step that triggers iterative plan revision before execution.
planning_integration: Retrieve-then-plan with an iterative predict-and-refine loop. Pipeline (Algorithm 1): retrieve top-k state/task experiences -> LLM analyze_experiences (insights) -> LLM generate_plan -> loop{ retrieve similar plans -> analyze_outcomes -> if predicted success break, else revise_plan } -> execute_plan -> add new experience to database. Closed loop: observe, retrieve, synthesize, act, log.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-plan / per-sub-task: retrieval and outcome-prediction are interleaved at the granularity of generating and revising a high-level plan for the current sub-task (before execution), not per CoT-token or per individual low-level action.
retrieved_item_representation: Raw natural-language experience tuples (state, task, plan, outcome paragraphs) injected verbatim into the prompt, supplemented by LLM-distilled free-text insights derived from them. Experiences are deliberately natural language rather than vectors or symbolic representations.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Raw natural-language trajectory/experience (state-task-plan-outcome case), additionally abstracted at use-time into distilled strategy/insight statements (e.g., causal rules like 'stone tools are prerequisites for iron mining') by the LLM analysis step.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Outcome-prediction-based self-validation: before execution, the system predicts the proposed plan's likely outcome from similar past plans and iteratively revises plans predicted to fail, which guards against acting on misleading retrieved context. The LLM insight-analysis step also serves to filter/interpret retrieved experiences. No retriever-aware training or explicit distractor-aware SFT.
memory_type: Episodic experience memory (natural-language (state,task,plan,outcome) experience database). Framed as a persistent 'mental model'.
write_back: True. After executing a plan, the new experience tuple (s_t, t_t, p_t, outcome) is added to the database D for future retrieval (Algorithm 1: D.add(...)).
online_growth: Yes. The store grows during deployment/test-time as the agent executes tasks; the continuous-building experiment shows the database expanding from 26 entries (Wooden Door) to 355 entries (Minecart) without resetting between tasks.
write_back_trigger: On every executed episode (success and failure alike): after plan execution the resulting experience tuple, including failure descriptions in the outcome field, is stored. Writes occur per executed plan/sub-task outcome rather than only on success or only after explicit self-critique.
failure_experience_usage: Success and failure both stored and retrieved. The outcome field explicitly records the execution result and a failure description if applicable; the LLM analyzes retrieved experiences specifically to identify 'common failure modes to avoid' (e.g., 'wooden pickaxes break mining iron'), enabling counterfactual/corrective reasoning from negative experiences.
memory_evolution_update: Append-only. New experience tuples are added to the FAISS index; the paper describes no dedup-merge, delta-update, refine-overwrite, or pruning of existing entries (it notes future work on experience pruning and hierarchical memory as a limitation).
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No. Retrieval/case-selection is a fixed weighted-similarity top-k over off-the-shelf embeddings, not a learned or RL-optimized policy.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No. Single-agent private experience database; no sharing across multiple agents or heterogeneous frameworks.
benchmarks: MineDojo (Minecraft simulation environment, Fan et al. 2022). 53 Minecraft tasks across 8 complexity tiers MT1-MT8 (MT1 Basic, MT2 Tool, MT3 Hunt and Food, MT4 Dig-down, MT5 Equipment, MT6 Tool-Complex, MT7 IronStage, MT8 Challenge/Diamond), grouped into Basic (MT1-MT2), Intermediate (MT3-MT5), Advanced (MT6-MT8). Observation space: RGB view, GPS, inventory; 42 discrete actions. Behavior-cloning controller (MineCLIP-based) trained on human demonstrations.
baselines: DEPS (Describe-Explain-Plan-Select; Wang et al. 2024c) — primary baseline, using the authors' own DEPS implementation without the experience database for fair comparison; Voyager (Wang et al. 2023); Reflexion (Shinn et al. 2023). Single-Shot (DEPS without iterative refinement) and No-Experience (retrieval removed) serve as internal ablation baselines.
key_metrics: Success Rate (% task completion across 30 trials); Learning Efficiency / Novel Learning Iterations (iterations or time-steps to skill mastery); Complexity Scaling (success vs MT tier); Retrieval Impact (success rate vs k); Continuous Learning (steps per task as the database grows).
headline_result: 9.4% mean improvement in open-world planning success rate over DEPS across MineCraft tasks (MT1-MT8), with the largest gains on intermediate-complexity tasks (e.g., +20.0% on MT3 Painting: 96.7% vs 76.7%; +11.0% average across intermediate tasks). Both systems reach 0% on the MT8 diamond task.
ablations: (1) No Experience: removing the retrieval/experience component reduces the method to DEPS-like single-shot planning, removing the gains. (2) Fixed k values (k=1,3,5,10,20): k=5 found optimal overall; simple tasks improve steadily with k while complex tasks need larger k, and advanced tasks (Minecart, Diamond) remain near-unachievable regardless of k. (3) Single-Shot: disabling iterative plan refinement (i.e., DEPS) lowers success. Also the field-weight choice (lambda_s=0.4, lambda_t=0.4, lambda_p=0.2) was set via these studies. Table 4 isolates the effect of outcome prediction (MINDSTORES with prediction vs DEPS without) per tier.
evaluation_decoupling: No. Only end-to-end task metrics (success rate, learning iterations, steps) are reported; no intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k / nDCG / retrieval completeness) are reported separately. Retrieval is examined only indirectly via success-rate-vs-k curves.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome metrics (task success rate). Some process-adjacent efficiency metrics are reported: novel-learning iterations to mastery and time-steps/steps-to-completion (Tables 3 and 4, Figures 4 and 6), which capture learning/planning efficiency but not reasoning faithfulness or step-wise retrieval accuracy.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Reports learning-efficiency gains: on Mine Iron, MINDSTORES needs 276 iterations vs Voyager/Reflexion capped at 500+; Make Stone Sword 187 vs 263 vs 500. Continuous-building experiment: completing Minecart took only ~9,112 total steps including the previous 9 tasks (~200 new steps) vs ~6,000 steps from scratch, with 100% success across the sequence; new-task step counts grow sub-linearly with complexity (Wooden Door 3,000; Furnace 4,879; Iron Pickaxe 8,598). Stated limitation: computational overhead scales with database size. No explicit API-cost/latency or per-retrieval-call cost numbers reported. [uncertain] on monetary/latency cost.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed-k injection: k=5 retrieved experiences (optimal) injected into the LLM prompt, with field-weighted similarity (state 0.4, task 0.4, plan 0.2); k swept over {1,3,5,10,20} in ablations. No explicit token budget cap or reranked-then-truncated strategy reported; selection count is a fixed k rather than adaptive/precision-driven. [uncertain] on exact prompt token budget.
builds_on: DEPS (Describe, Explain, Plan and Select; Wang et al. 2024c) — MINDSTORES keeps DEPS's iterative verbal-feedback planning foundation and adds a persistent experience database. MineDojo (Fan et al. 2022) environment and MineCLIP/behavior-cloning controller. Sentence-BERT (all-MiniLM-L6-v2) embeddings and FAISS for retrieval. GPT-4 as the LLM planner/reasoner. Conceptually grounded in Craik's (1952) mental-models theory.
contrasts_with: Zero-shot/no-memory LLM planners that start fresh each episode (DEPS, ProgPrompt, Inner Monologue); skill-library/code-memory agents with opaque, non-interpretable representations (Voyager's code snippets, PaLM-E's latent vectors); feedback-loop agents lacking persistent cross-episode memory (Reflexion, ReAct); memory-augmented planners with shallow/non-causal reasoning evaluated mainly on narrow benchmarks like ALFRED (ExpeL, E2CL, AdaPlanner); latent/symbolic world-model and tree-search methods (PIGLeT, RAP, DreamerV3, LATS).
lineage: Group C (RAG planning): experience/memory-augmented LLM planning for embodied agents. Sits in the lineage of zero-shot LLM open-world planners (Inner Monologue -> DEPS -> Voyager) extended with growing episodic natural-language experience memory; closely related to experiential-learner memory planners (Reflexion, ExpeL, AdaPlanner, E2CL), distinguished by storing interpretable (state,task,plan,outcome) NL tuples retrieved for plan refinement and outcome prediction in an open-world (MineDojo) setting.
cbr_cycle_coverage: Realizes a Retrieve-Reuse-Retain CBR cycle without naming it: Retrieve (top-k similar (s,t,p,o) experiences), Reuse (LLM adapts retrieved cases/insights into a new plan), Retain (writes the new experience tuple back). Revise is present as plan refinement via outcome prediction but operates on the new plan rather than mutating stored cases. Flags: [Retrieve: yes, Reuse: yes, Revise: partial (new-plan revision, not stored-case revision), Retain: yes].
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The paper does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza or Kolodner; it is framed via cognitive 'mental models' (Craik 1952) and 'experience-augmented planning'. It realizes CBR-like mechanisms under different terminology.
tool_document_engineering: N/A (no tool/skill retrieval; experiences are NL episode tuples, not tool/API documents).
index_content_separation: N/A. No lightweight-index-vs-heavy-content separation; the embedded NL experience tuples are both the index keys and the retrieved content.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A (no external tool index or integration protocol; not a tool-retrieval system).
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A as a tool-retrieval mechanism. (Task/crafting dependencies such as 'stone pickaxe before iron mining' are handled implicitly by the LLM reasoning over retrieved experiences and insights, not via an explicit dependency graph over retrievable tools.)
adaptation_mechanism: LLM-prompted adaptation plus prediction-driven revision: the LLM synthesizes insights from retrieved cases and generates a plan (case reuse/adaptation), then iteratively revises the plan based on predicted outcomes from similar past plans before execution (a predicted-feedback-driven revision, not execution-feedback within the same loop and not RL fine-tuning).
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (not a benchmark paper; it uses MineDojo's existing tasks). For reference, it evaluates on 53 MineCraft tasks across MT1-MT8, 30 trials each, episodes 3,000-12,000 steps; best-system difficulty signal: MT8 diamond = 0% for all methods, indicating the hardest tasks remain unsolved.
